task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: primary play types of the absent player
same-position minutes as a similarity basis
methodological_questions: Can the teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile be identified in a way that is defined once, before analysis?
Is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types the same teammate that was closest before the absence?
Do 11 cases and 148 spells provide enough independent information to test a teammate-ranking claim?
How much of any post-absence gain is explained by regression to the mean, minutes increases, or roster and lineup changes rather than by profile similarity?
evidence_establishes: The retrieval returned no earlier study-family records, so no prior result on this question, or on closely related teammate-redistribution questions, is available in this setting.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether closest-profile teammates absorb the absent player's initiations in any prior sample.
Whether 11 cases are sufficient for a ranking test.
Whether the 'closest profile' definition is stable across measures.
Any effect size, direction, or base rate for post-absence usage gains.
own_inferences: The question has three competing operational definitions (closest initiation profile, most minutes, most initiations, or same-position minutes). Testing all of them against the same outcome is a multiplicity problem and would allow the analyst to choose the definition that gives the answer wanted.

The 'largest gainer' target is partly mechanical. Teammates with the most minutes or initiations after an absence will mechanically gain more initiations, so a profile-based claim has to be compared against a minutes-only baseline.

148 spells from 11 cases are not 148 independent observations. Spells within a case share the same absent player, team, season and roster context, so the effective sample is closer to 11 cases, which gives very little power for a ranking claim.

The per-game play-by-play and the derived initiator records use the same source, so the outcome (initiations by play type) and the profile measure are partly derived from the same labels. This raises the chance that measurement error or attribution rules drive the result.
uncertainties: Whether the derived play-type initiator labels are reliable enough for play-type attribution.
How many of the 11 cases have a clean absence window with enough pre- and post-absence possessions to estimate a profile.
The exact definition of 'primary types' and how many play types qualify per absent player.
Whether the 2025-26 partial data will be complete when the analysis is run, since the playoffs are complete only from 2026-06-21.

historical_effect.explanation: No earlier records were returned, so the decision rests on the task description and general design considerations, not on prior results. The empty retrieval neither supports nor rules out the question.

blocking_constraints.text: With 11 cases, a ranking claim about which teammate is the largest gainer cannot reach useful power; spells are not independent units.
Many absence spells may have too few post-absence initiations per play type to estimate a per-teammate gain reliably.
Minutes-based gains are partly mechanical, so the largest gainer is likely the highest-minutes teammate regardless of profile similarity.
The profile measure and the outcome both come from play-by-play initiator labels, so they share measurement error and attribution rules.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved (retrieve_history returned 0 results), so it cannot be said whether this question has been answered. The status is unknown, not no.

risks.text: 11 cases give very little power; spells within a case are correlated and should not be treated as independent.

The probability that a randomly chosen teammate is the largest gainer is low when many teammates are eligible; the base rate for a profile-based match is unknown and should be estimated from the data before any claim.
High-minutes teammates gain initiations mechanically, which can make a profile claim look supported without any profile effect.
Absences are often chosen because a player was having an unusual period or was injured after a usage peak, so post-absence usage shifts partly reflect regression to the mean.
Lineup, starter status, coach or game-plan changes and opponent quality can move usage at the same time as the absence.
Initiator and play-type attribution from play-by-play can be wrong, which would misassign gains to the wrong teammate.
Profile and outcome are both derived from the same play-by-play initiator records, which creates shared-error dependence.

Several profile definitions (initiation profile, minutes, initiations, same-position minutes) and several play types give many comparisons; choosing the best one after seeing results inflates false positives.
Without placebo teammates or placebo absence windows, a 'largest gainer' result cannot be separated from ordinary roster reshuffling.
Play-style and usage trends across 2022-23 to 2025-26 can change gains independently of the absence.

design.estimand: As posed, the claim is not a single estimand: it names a ranking of teammates by gain in the absent player's primary play types. The minimum viable estimand is the difference in post-absence initiation share gain between the one pre-registered closest-profile teammate and the highest-minutes teammate, per absence case, reported descriptively.
design.unit: Absence case (player-team-season absence window). Spells are nested within cases and are not independent units.
design.sample: Only cases with a clean absence window and enough pre- and post-absence initiations per primary play type. The count is at most 11 cases and is likely smaller after filtering.
design.power: Not achievable for a confirmatory ranking test with 11 cases. Report a descriptive analysis with uncertainty intervals and treat any test as exploratory.
design.controls: Use a minutes-only baseline, adjust for pre-absence usage trend (regression-to-the-mean check using matched non-absent periods), starter status, lineup changes and opponent strength. Use placebo absence windows for the same teammates.
design.falsification: Compare the closest-profile teammate against placebo windows where no absence occurred. If the same teammate gains equally in placebo windows, the effect is not attributable to the absence.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register one profile definition, one primary play-type set and one primary outcome. Report all other definitions as secondary and exploratory with correction.
design.decision_rule: Only a pre-registered descriptive comparison is reported. Claim support only if the closest-profile teammate beats both the minutes-only baseline and the placebo windows with intervals excluding zero, which is unlikely at this sample size. Otherwise report as uncertain.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs complete; 2025-26 regular season only after 2026-04-13 and playoffs only after 2026-06-21. Freeze the data version and record the cut-off date before analysis.
